papers.title: Sada-ASR: A Production Multidialectal Arabic Speech Recognition System
papers.abstract: Callers to Arabic customer-service lines speak their own dialect, while speech recognizers are built and evaluated mainly on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). A recognizer that mishears the dialect breaks the call before anything else can help. We present Sada-ASR, the speech recognizer of EchoNova's production Arabic voice agent. On a 120-hour test set of MSA and eight dialects, it has the lowest word and character error rates of twelve systems, against eleven from Microsoft, ElevenLabs, Google, OpenAI, Speechmatics, IFM, Cohere, NVIDIA and Audar: 11.69% word error rate against 13.51% for the strongest, Microsoft's MAI-Transcribe-2 (a lead of 0.74 points on clips unaffected by that system's fixed number and script conventions), and 15.52% against 16.96% averaged over varieties. Its largest margins are on Omani (4.30 points), Egyptian (3.78) and Saudi (2.19) speech; it is level on Syrian and

papers.title: CLEW: Log-Anchored Backward Tracing for Root-Cause Code Localization
papers.abstract: Failures in industrial software systems may involve multiple components and be difficult to reproduce outside the production environment. Root-cause code localization therefore often relies on issue descriptions and runtime logs. However, log evidence may be noisy or incomplete, and the code reporting a symptom may differ from the code containing the underlying defect. These conditions make it challenging to identify relevant log evidence and determine which functions could have caused the reported failure. To address this gap, we introduce CLEW, an agentic approach that combines rule-based log-to-code anchoring with LLM-guided backward code tracing. CLEW organizes selected observations into diagnostic states, guides source exploration from anchored symptom functions, and returns ranked candidate functions, an affected module, and an explanation comprising a proposed mechanism path and a

papers.title: Are Revealed Preferences All You Need for AI Alignment?
papers.abstract: AI agents learn what principals want from what principals choose. We offer a criterion for when a principal's decisions, at every belief an AI might hold, are all the AI needs. For acting, they are. Cautious actions, such as deferring to a person, typically divide the principal's actions into blocks, and for choosing costless evidence, decisions are enough exactly when the same evidence is best in every block. Otherwise, the AI acts as its principal would yet can gather the wrong evidence, and greater capability can turn that error into incorrect actions. Choices between two mistakes reveal what decisions miss.

papers.title: One Run Is Not Enough: Reminding a small Gemma 4 coding agent of its last finding made no measurable difference in a paired test
papers.abstract: When a coding agent runs out of room, its earlier findings are cut and it forgets them. We tested a simple fix: automatically putting the agent's last finding back in front of it. We fixed the rules in advance and ran 98 paired coding tasks with and without this reminder, using Gemma 4 31B (QAT, 4-bit) in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent harness. The reminder made no measurable difference: across all 98 tasks, 47 were solved with it and 48 without (-1.0 points, 95% interval [-8.3, +6.3], exact McNemar p=1.0). The primary outcome (a documented deviation from our preregistration), the first 48 pairs, was 29/48 with memory against 25/48 without (+8.3 points, [-2.1, +18.3], p=0.22); the extension of 50 tasks, decided after that result, pointed the other way (18/50 against 23/50, -10.0 points, p=0.125), so the sign did not replicate. papers.title: Optional Traps: An Empirical Study of LLM Agents Against Credential Deception and Alert-Driven Revocation
papers.abstract: Deception (honeypots, decoys and canary credentials) rests on a simple premise: legitimate users never touch a fake asset, so any touch is a high-confidence signal. We ask whether that premise holds when the attacker is a large language model (LLM) agent, and what deception contributes once ordinary hardening is in place. We built an isolated, hash-chained lab around a mock Records API and report four studies. (1) In an exploratory run, a local 9.7B-parameter model ignored every optional decoy, read a genuinely leaked service key from a debug endpoint and exported the protected records in both static and adaptive deception modes. (2) After removing the leak, planting a canary credential in its place and revoking the offending client, a frozen 60-session study with a 4B-parameter model found export success of 20/20 at baseline, 0/20 with hardening alone and 0/20 with hardening plus decept

papers.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. papers.title: Read Boundaries in Agent Memory: Consistency, Completeness, and Repair
papers.abstract: Agent-memory services assemble evidence through several reads across connections or stores. An update between those reads can pair an assertion with source content from another revision. We protect the complete recall, including enrichment and materialization, and evaluate the resulting evidence and service behavior in Hindsight and Cognee. A 600-run Cognee study compares unprotected recall, a repeated recall, a read/write lock, and optimistic epoch validation under default incremental updates and full rebuilds. At approximately 20 recalls/s, unprotected default updates yield 199 conflicting responses among 12,010 scheduled recalls with spaced writes and 284 among 12,010 with bursts. The lock and epoch validation each deliver complete, compatible evidence for all 24,020 default-update recalls. papers.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. papers.title: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
papers.abstract: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x faster than the benchmark's reference baseline. The search starts from zero: agents get each problem's PyTorch definition but no reference kernels or official scores. A per-problem archive outside the model holds every correct kernel and its lineage. An LLM controller reads it, picks a parent or a new design, and gives each parallel child agent one direction. papers.title: Feedback-Aware Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Timely Communication in Cognitive Radio Networks
papers.abstract: Supporting time-sensitive services in cognitive radio networks requires distributed access strategies that translate shared spectrum opportunities into timely packet delivery. Achieving this objective is challenging because reception conditions are only partially observable to individual transmitters, while dynamic competition and access overhead constrain the service that can be completed within packet deadlines. We formulate a distributed access problem that captures the coupling among interference-dependent reception, queue evolution, and protocol durations. To address this problem, we propose feedback-aware residual multi-agent proximal policy optimization (FAR-MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution. papers.title: Self-Calibrating Vision-Agent-Action: Deploying Pick-and-Place to New Robot Cells without Demonstrations or Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: In simulation, Vision-Agent-Action (VAA) performs pick-and-place in robot cells with gripper or base-frame changes without robot demonstrations or fine-tuning. It uses pre-trained vision-language and language models for interpretation, measures the command map and camera geometry from its own motion and fingertips, estimates lens distortion, and plans grasps from measured object depth. A controlled study of eight public LIBERO-fine-tuned vision-language-action models (VLAs) varies robot hardware, camera geometry, appearance, and base frame. Gripper and frame changes dominate their losses in the tested fractional design. Across 18 cells with these changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%). papers.title: Ego2Sim2Humanoid: Agentic Real-to-Sim for Learning Loco-Manipulation VLAs without Robot Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies on teleoperated robot demonstrations, which are costly because every episode requires a trained operator controlling a physical robot in real time through teleoperation interfaces and wearable body-tracking hardware. Egocentric glasses capture human demonstrations without a robot or handheld grippers, yet they track only the head and in-view human hands, and directly copying human motion to a robot with different stature, arm reach and hand morphology fails to produce feasible contacts. \method{} converts egocentric glasses recordings into physically verified robot training trajectories. An agentic real-to-sim stage reconstructs collision and textured visual assets from the recorded RGB-D and head streams, completes unseen surfaces when needed, and predicts target contact bands on the manipulated objects. papers.title: A Unified Control Framework, Mathematical Model, and Five-layer Closed-loop Case Study for Embodied Intelligence Control Systems
papers.abstract: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition and behavior through real-time body-environment interaction, so its control system must tightly couple perception, decision making, learning, optimization, constraints, and physical execution. This report asks whether a unified framework exists, how its mathematical models unify, and how the framework is realized computably. Four conclusions emerge. (1) No single framework is accepted, but the field converges on a common skeleton: from operational-space and whole-body control to MPC, reinforcement learning, active inference, and diffusion/flow policies, all reduce to constrained sequential decision making on the configuration manifold. papers.title: Conditional Endorsement: Simulating How Adults with Different Skills Evaluate Canada's National AI Strategy
papers.abstract: Canada's 2026 national AI strategy, AI for All, commits to free AI training for everyone and to expanding business AI adoption, yet it is difficult to anticipate whether these policies will reach adults with uneven skills and circumstances. We ask how adults with diverse skills might rate these policies on support, effectiveness, and personal benefit, how their skills and circumstances shape these evaluations, and what implementation conditions they raise. We built 3,200 generative agents from a weighted sample of the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Cycle 2 respondents, collected their ratings and explanations for 20 policies, and analyzed dialogues between agents with contrasting ratings. The agents supported nearly every policy but were far less confident that they would improve adult AI literacy or benefit them personally. This gap widened as d

papers.title: More Context, Mixed Results: Evaluating LLMs for Identifier Recovery and Code Deobfuscation
papers.abstract: Source code is often obfuscated through identifier renaming, incentivizing reverse engineers to develop techniques for recovering meaningful names. To assess how LLMs compare with these techniques, we evaluate 4 traditional baselines and 3 LLMs (Qwen, OLMo and DeepSeek) on identifier detection and semantic recovery across 51 recent Java projects, 3 obfuscators, and 6 context/retrieval settings. LLMs generally outperform traditional techniques on both tasks, but benefit from different forms of context and settings: agentic retrieval yields the strongest detection results, reaching 91.56% $F_1$, while enclosing-class context generally improves semantic recovery at a higher token cost. Despite these gains, exact recovery peaks at 16.42% overall (under one-hop context) and 32.93% for field names (under repository retrieval), which are the easiest to recover. papers.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
papers.abstract: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. When: stronger critics attenuate the loss on the evaluated suite, without establishing a universal capability threshold. papers.title: Personalized Language Models for One-to-Many Private Communications
papers.abstract: We study relationship-specific continual reply prediction for one-to-many private communication: a system predicts an author's reply to a recurring contact and updates its personalization state when the actual reply becomes available. We propose TRACE (Temporal Relationship-Aware Communication Evolution), which uses author-level lexical habits, contact-specific wording, and temporal expression estimates to guide a frozen language model, with a feedback-driven policy controlling revision. On 216 test emails from eight Enron users, all four main TRACE configurations achieve higher mean BLEU, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore and lower mean Reply Style MSE than Base LLM and Base RAG. Component ablations show mixed effects and do not establish statistically reliable improvements in Reply Style MSE after multiple-comparison correction. More accurate state forecasts and larger revision budgets do not con

papers.title: How Diverse Are Layered Safeguards? Estimands and Measurement for Ensembles of LLM Jailbreak Defenses
papers.abstract: Practitioners protect large language models (LLMs) by stacking safeguards: a likelihood filter, a guard classifier, hidden-state probes, a decoding-time intervention. Such a stack is an ensemble of learned detectors, and ensemble theory states when combination pays: when members fail on different inputs. Stacking is recommended throughout the LLM security literature, but this condition has not been measured for any pair of safeguards. The condition is three quantities, not one, and conflating them is why it has resisted measurement. Separately optimized attacks license only a claim about which \emph{behaviors} are jointly vulnerable; the identity that governs a deployed stack is written over shared \emph{inputs}; and neither predicts what an adversary attacking the assembled pipeline achieves. papers.title: Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
papers.abstract: Komi-Zyrian, Moksha, Erzya and Udmurt have mature rule-based resources, among them finite-state analysers, constraint grammars and bilingual dictionaries, which language models do not use. We ask whether giving a model access to these resources improves machine translation from the four languages into English, and whether it matters how the access is provided: as analyses computed in advance and written into the prompt, or as tools that the model calls itself through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We evaluate manually: an expert linguist read every English output of the strongest model under three conditions, 816 sentences in all, accepted or rejected each one, and named the main error in every rejected translation. With the analyses in the prompt, the number of accepted translations rises from 13 to 43 out of 272; with the tools attached it rises to 55. The gain comes from the biling

papers.title: ROUNDS: Source-Framed Diagnostic Revision after Multi-Turn Clinical Evidence
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competing diagnoses in written five-clinician panels. Across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets, average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options a

papers.title: Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
papers.abstract: Business process redesign (BPR) has a long-standing catalog of best-practice redesign heuristics, yet, applying them remains a mostly manual task that requires extensive domain knowledge. Despite recent advances using Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational process model redesign, limitations remain. For example, redesign is user-driven instead of data-driven and is not guided by best practices such as the redesign heuristics. Moreover, only one change can be handled at a time. To address these limitations, given an event log and a BPMN model, we present the DH-BPR framework to realize data-driven heuristic-guided BPR using LLMs. To design DH-BPR, we first conducted an analysis of which redesign heuristics can be automatically detected and applied given information contained in an event log such as the fraction of cases that bypass an activity. Based on this, DH-BPR detects and v

papers.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce PBit1, a finite-control representation of pretrained neural networks that assigns one programmable p-bit to each learned parameter. A 12-bit command sets its probability, a shared affine range maps that probability to the weight domain, and temporal observations reconstruct the weight for inference. Operator-aware range grouping and sensitivity-based sampling allocation adapt the representation to the network. Across five independent weight draws at 32,768 observations per scalar, selected configurations preserve task quality in GPT-2, DistilBERT, and LFM3-1.7B with every learned scalar converted and no fine-tuning. GPT-2 and LFM3 perplexity increase by approximately 0.66% and 0.26%, respectively, while DistilBERT accuracy changes from 87.51% to 87.49%. A sensitivity-based policy reduces GPT-2 reconstruction observations by 41.7% while retaining the quality criterion. Comple

papers.title: Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
papers.abstract: Post-hoc explanations of deep-learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are difficult to trust because different attribution methods highlight different retinal regions for the same image, and a visually plausible heatmap does not show that the highlighted pixels drive the prediction. We propose the Consensus-Calibrated Explanation Map (CCEM), which fuses Grad-CAM++, Ada-SISE, and SmoothGrad Integrated Gradients (SG-IG) using image-specific weights derived from annotation-free reliability cues: deletion sensitivity, inter-method agreement, compactness, retinal containment, and peak structure. CCEM explains a frozen ordinal grader, an EfficientNet-B7 with CBAM and a scalar regression head, pre-trained on EyePACS 2015 in Stage 1 and fine-tuned on APTOS 2019 in Stage 2 with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK)-optimized thresholds; it reaches a QWK of 0.920 on the hidden Kaggle test s

papers.title: Evaluating and Improving Natural Language Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Natural language autoencoders (NLAs) are a method for generating natural language explanations of LLM activations. We develop evaluations based on auditing tasks that test the ability of NLAs to surface latent knowledge, identify whether a model was misled by a hint, and catch a silent fabrication. We also develop extensions to NLAs that let them use activation information from multiple layers and positions, let us apply them more effectively to long transcripts, and reduce the number of false claims they make. These extensions result in improvements on both our auditing evaluations and auxiliary evaluations adapted from prior work. We also use the evaluations to study how different auditing capabilities change over the course of NLA training, and find that although every evaluation improves early in training, extended training can hurt performance on some of our auditing evaluations.

papers.title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
papers.abstract: Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) to construct executable programs through environment interaction, feedback analysis, and code revision. However, prior work has mainly treated LLMs as optimizers, overlooking their ability to transfer knowledge across system levels. We propose Program Distillation (PD), a framework that formalizes the transfer of abilities from System 2 to System 0. During learning, the LLM provides task knowledge and draft strategies; at deployment, a student program executes the resulting policy. We show that this approach can improve performance while reducing inference time. We introduce PDBench, a benchmark comprising 27 discrete- and continuous-control tasks with fixed initial policies, and PDMetaHarness, a model-harness-independent meta-system for monitoring and guiding the learning process. papers.title: CausalGloss: Multi-Evidence Action Control for a Simultaneous Mandarin Speech-to-ASL Gloss Cascade
papers.abstract: Simultaneous Mandarin speech-to-American Sign Language (ASL) gloss translation requires deciding when an evolving utterance supports committing each gloss. Fixed Wait-k cannot adapt to source-gloss reordering, while training only on reference histories causes exposure bias. We present CausalGloss, an English-prefix-to-ASL-gloss action policy for a Mandarin-speech cascade. It combines lexical and semantic evidence, bounded delay, negation constraints, burst WRITE actions, and incomplete-history recovery. On a frozen 500-example How2Sign-derived benchmark with weak LLM-generated references, CausalGloss improves the fixed Wait-k frontier and nearly matches a three-seed TransLLaMA-style learned adaptive baseline at k = 5 in Token F1 (0.7047 versus 0.7067), with 54.4% lower LAAL. Against CLERC Epee human-gloss references, it achieves 0.649 Token F1 and Pareto-dominates three-seed TransLLaMA-s

papers.title: A Comparative Evaluation of BERT-Based and LLM-Based Models for Indic Sentence Similarity
papers.abstract: The relative effectiveness of BERT-based encoders and large language model (LLM)-based embeddings for Indic semantic textual similarity remains insufficiently characterized. We compare eight BERT-based and five LLM-based models on the 1,500-pair STS Benchmark development set translated into ten Indic languages and on the native Marathi MahaSTS test set. IndicSBERT achieves the highest Pearson correlation in all ten translated language sets, with a macro-average of 0.843, followed by BGE-M3 at 0.792. Harrier-270M is the strongest LLM-based model on translated STS-B, with a macro-average of 0.751. On MahaSTS, IndicSBERT and Bhasha-Embed-v0 achieve Pearson correlations of 0.901 and 0.900, respectively, while EmbeddingGemma leads the LLM-based models at 0.871. The highest-scoring BERT-based model thus exceeds the highest-scoring LLM-based model in both settings, although the magnitude of the

papers.title: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to collaboratively adapt to distributed private data. However, long-context fine-tuning on resource-constrained devices faces substantial challenges arising from excessive activation memory, heterogeneous token-importance patterns across clients, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose SMELL, a Sparsity-aware and Memory-Efficient federated fine-tuning framework for Long-context LLMs. SMELL integrates three complementary mechanisms: Local Sparse-Forward Adaptation (LSFA), Consensus-Anchored Sparsity Coordination (CASC), and Communication-Efficient Progressive Update Recovery (CPUR). These mechanisms jointly enable memory-efficient local adaptation, heterogeneity-aware sparsity coordination, and lightweight model-update transmission. Experiments on OPT-350M and LLaMA2-7B demonstrate that SMELL reduces pe

papers.title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) enables sample-efficient search for expensive black-box problems, but its performance depends strongly on surrogate-acquisition configurations whose suitability varies across problems and optimization states. We take a significant step toward LLM-driven strategic management of BO with STaSBO, a task-agnostic meta-controller that plans search behavior and jointly selects surrogate-acquisition configurations, while numerical BO retains responsibility for probabilistic modeling and candidate generation. STaSBO comprises two coordinated stages: strategy planning and strategy-guided configuration selection. A structured memory system connects prior plans, configuration selections, and candidate behaviors to optimization states, allowing the controller to revise its trajectory summary and behavioral plans during planning. To navigate the large joint configuration spa

papers.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
papers.abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolv

papers.title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
papers.abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handw

papers.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. We organize the literature by the primary resource the LLM manages: artifact-centric methods for computational artifacts, operational-centric methods for deployment context and system state, and resource-centric methods for data and energy. These categories span the lifecycle and cover AI-specific concerns such as distributed-training configuration, inference serving, GPU-cluster scheduling, a

papers.title: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly read a scene and report it to someone who acts on the report, sometimes under objectives that differ from that person's. We ask whether a stated incentive moves what a VLM reports, and whether this changes when the value must be read from pixels rather than given as text. In seeded synthetic scenes, a model reads the position of a target on a labelled axis and reports one integer to a fixed receiver; it is paid, in simulation, for accuracy or for a report a few units to one side, and every scene is also presented with the true value as text. Across a pilot and three follow-up studies with hash-frozen protocols, four small open VLMs from three families, and 15,170 held-out trials, a stated payoff moved reports in both modalities, and exact compliance at three units was significantly lower with the image than with text for three of four models; Qw

papers.title: From zero-target transfer to target-site personalization: multi-source training across fall-detection models
papers.abstract: Video-based fall detection could support timely assistance when a person cannot call for help. Unfamiliar cameras and scarce local labels challenge deployment. We examine whether joint training improves cross-dataset detection and subsequent local training. We analyze 2,697 clips from eight OmniFall datasets and one AI-Hub dataset. Positive clips contain a fall or collapse transition, while negative clips do not. We hold out each dataset in turn, training on the other eight. We evaluate three vision-language models (VLMs), Qwen, LLaVA, and InternVL, and three visual baselines, CLIP-temporal, VideoMAE, and Pose-TCN. We evaluate the stored source model without target data for training or selection. For each label budget, we update a separate copy using labeled clips from the held-out target dataset. We call this target-site personalization. We compare the Source-initialized model with Targ

papers.title: Learning Spatially Aware Audio-Visual Features from Videos with Mono Audio
papers.abstract: Comprehensive audio-visual perception requires both semantic and spatial reasoning. Existing spatial models suffer from poor generalization due to data scarcity, while semantic-only models fail to capture spatial characteristics completely. We introduce a model capable of jointly reasoning over binaural audio and vision on semantic and spatial tasks with improved generalization. To overcome the shortage in real-world data, we develop an automatic pipeline that localizes the sound source in a video, estimates its relative 3D trajectory, and renders binaural audio. We then use this to spatialize VGGSound, allowing us to train at a much larger scale. We demonstrate improved performance and generalization on spatial reasoning tasks while still remaining competitive on semantic tasks compared to semantic-only models.

papers.title: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
papers.abstract: Matrix-structured optimizers can improve language-model pretraining, but it is unclear whether these gains transfer to short-horizon KL distillation from an instruction-tuned initialization. We compare AdamW and diagonal AdaGrad with two tractable Shampoo reductions, SOAP, and All-2D Muon across four dense Qwen student-teacher pairs under a common forward-KL objective and fixed training budget. Across scales, none of the evaluated matrix-structured recipes consistently improves the quality versus trainer-time trade-off over the elementwise references: AdamW generally attains the lowest validation KL, while AdaGrad can be slightly faster at larger scale. SOAP often tracks AdamW in KL but incurs substantial trainer-time overhead, and the two Shampoo reductions reverse ordering across model pairs, showing that conclusions depend on the feasible recipe. These results suggest that pretraining

papers.title: Real-World End-to-End Product Entity Resolution
papers.abstract: Product Entity Resolution (PER) in e-commerce is challenging due to unstructured text, formatting inconsistencies, promotional noise, and fine-grained product differences. We present an end-to-end evaluation of four zero-shot PER pipelines---Lexical Cascade, Semantic Cascade, Hybrid Fusion Cascade, and Generative-Lexical Cascade---across established benchmarks and introduce two real-world datasets characterized by cross-lingual noise and dense brand collisions. We evaluate lexical and dense blocking with cross-encoder, tensor-search, and Large Language Model verification, considering accuracy, runtime, and memory consumption.

papers.title: Hardware-Friendly Plug-and-Play MVDR Beamforming for Microphone Arrays: Algorithm, Prototype, and System-Level Feasibility
papers.abstract: Beamforming has been widely recognized for its spatial filtering capability in speech signal processing, enabling effective interference rejection and signal enhancement. The performance of adaptive beamforming methods, e.g., the conventional minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming, often deteriorate significantly in complex and dynamic acoustic environments. Part of the reason is that such conventional beamforming ignores the intrinsic characteristics of speech. To address this issue, this paper proposes Plug-and-Play Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (PnP-MVDR) algorithm, which integrates data-driven speech prior information into the MVDR framework to enhance robustness against non-stationary noise while maintaining its interpretability. The PnP-MVDR framework supports joint interaction of signal processing and deep learning methods and is designed to be comp

papers.title: Operating-Point Failure of Frozen Guardrail Probes Under Backbone Updates
papers.abstract: We freeze a guardrail probe and threshold, then measure its operating point across 18 cells covering 16 public language-model updates. At a 1% target, the threshold fails closed in 8 of 9 cells in the first phase and either fails closed or open in 3 of 9 cells in a registered second phase (descriptive). The two phases also differ in update type and input format. The largest increase is from 1.01% to 15.12%, while the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve changes by no more than 0.0058 in any of these cells. A benchmark's staleness criteria classify none of them as stale. A rule based on these criteria flags 0.019 of layer cells where the rate doubles or halves. A label-free rate estimate flags 0.918, clearing 0.898 of the remaining cells. A two-moment model matches the change within a factor of 1.5 in 0.905 of 63 registered cells and in 0.773 of the 22 cells that moved.

papers.title: Empowering Masked Diffusion Models to Self-Correct with Leave-One-Out Transformers
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for language modeling, enabling parallel token generation with competitive performance. Yet standard MDMs suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) inability to revise tokens, and (2) sparse training signal. We revisit hollow transformers, which address both limitations by predicting each token from its surrounding context, independently of the input at that position. We introduce the Leave-One-Out Transformer (LOOT), a more efficient and expressive architecture that advances hollow transformers through two complementary advances. First, we redesign the merging mechanism to enable frequent interaction between left and right contexts, substantially improving predictive performance over prior hollow transformers. Second, we derive a lower-variance estimator of the MDM NELBO that supervises all tokens and improves valida

papers.title: A Nonlinear Abstract Domain for Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) explicitly model epistemic uncertainty by leveraging probability distributions over network parameters, making them better suited for risk-aware decision-making. Yet soundly propagating uncertainty through the network and capturing the entire output distribution to support predictive uncertainty quantification remains a fundamental challenge. Existing approaches are either sampling-based, providing no formal guarantees, or propagate only selected statistical properties, such as expectations and entropy, limiting their applicability to general probabilistic queries. To address these challenges, we present the first nonlinear abstract domain for soundly approximating complete probability distributions of BNNs. The abstract domain builds upon a novel marginal collecting concrete semantics that soundly abstracts the classical joint-measure semantics. It combin

papers.title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
papers.abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer, a compact hybrid state-space and attention architecture designed for early-life degradation trajectory forecasting. DecayFormer combines cycle-level

papers.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
papers.abstract: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria; and realistic interactive evaluation, where models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes. Reasoning-intensive

papers.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key miles

papers.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
papers.abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for di

papers.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
papers.abstract: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models and using 2.1M-3.8M training pairs from public datasets, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU) and rivals stat

papers.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. papers.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
papers.abstract: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of $432$ strictly paired test cases across $48$ executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a $3 \times 3$ factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. papers.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
papers.abstract: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically. Second, FOAM replaces SOAP's dense rotat

papers.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
papers.abstract: While search agents demonstrate impressive capabilities in multi-step question answering, their robustness to poor-quality evidence remains under-explored. Such evidence is rare in benchmark corpora, and resulting failures are hard to reproduce. We propose DeepStress, a dynamic stress-testing framework that subjects agents to degraded evidence at controlled rates. It replaces the retrieval module with a synthetic environment where documents are generated dynamically for each query, under independent control of their trustworthiness, relevance, and factuality. To characterize behavior under stress, we go beyond binary accuracy with a five-way classification of final-answer outcomes and two new reliability-aware metrics, RAS and CoPRAS, which credit cautious behavior and account for computational cost. Evaluating 12 systems on questions from HotpotQA and BrowseComp-Plus, we find that sever

papers.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
papers.abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises t

papers.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
papers.abstract: Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by reconstructing a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these videos and the long, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene reconstruction: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video. Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos. Each delivery is scored along two evaluation dimensions. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported 4D scene with hidden ground truth facts in nine dimensions. VLM-based Screen Check asks a VLM judge whether the facts that pass can be recognized in the proxy video. We analyze the evaluation results and trajectories of 11 fr

papers.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
papers.abstract: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the predicted future. The BEV, rendered from scene annotations for training, depicts roads and vehicles as simple shapes at a fixed metric scale, providing a top-down view of their positions and motion with reduce

papers.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
papers.abstract: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, wi

papers.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded canary deployment. We establish an evaluator-calibrated simultaneous lower-bound construction for a countable sequence of adaptively generated candid

papers.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. We want the best of both worlds: gradient updates from a scalar reward, while also utilizing environment information to hand off experience. As a concrete testbed, we fix the Agentic Context Engineering (\ace{}) harness and train one model to act, reflect, and curate task-local playbooks. Our method, \acerl{}, evaluates candidate experience-handoff artifacts by

papers.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
papers.abstract: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. \emph{Rather than deciding how much to think}, we explore a different paradigm, \emph{zero-or-$T$ thinking}: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of $T$ tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a \emph{hybrid decision model} (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight \emph{self-routing block} chooses between them. The block estimates the \emph{value of thinking}, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast one, from what that implicit thinking has already produced, and the slow mode runs only where that value exceeds a price $λ$ set per request. papers.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
papers.abstract: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments. A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and p

papers.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and d

papers.title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. In contrast with traditional 3D reconstruction, doing so requires satisfying discrete physical constraints, which provide structure but render the problem combinatorial and highly sensitive to small pose errors. To learn a prior over how parts fit together, we train a set-conditioned SE(3) flow model on procedurally generated assemblies. We then finetune this model to inject image conditioning, using 1% as much data. However, while the learned flow captures global structure, it does not enforce connectivity. To address this, we introduce an analytic connectivity-field guidance to pull predictions toward connected assemblies at test time. Through this, we demonstrate improved build quality with model size, pretraining, and guidance. We make our models and data

papers.title: EvenVLM: A Text and Multimodal Dataset for the Even Language with Vision-Language Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: We present EvenVLM, the first text and multimodal (VQA) dataset for Even (Lamut), an endangered Northern Tungusic language spoken by approximately 6,800 people in Siberia. Our dataset comprises 50,521 structured Even-Russian entries extracted from dictionary and phrasebook sources via GPT-4o Mini-based parsing, from which we synthetically generate 107,543 training examples spanning translation, grammar, reading comprehension, and semantic classification. To address tokenization inefficiency on Even's agglutinative morphology, we propose a three-step tokenizer expansion algorithm that adds Even-specific graphemes (eng, oe, o-umlaut), whitelisted vocabulary, and BPE merges, reducing average tokens per word by 27% (4.99 to 3.64). Using LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-4B, we adapt the model for text tasks (0.53% trainable parameters, rank 32) and separately for visual question answering (rank 6

papers.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
papers.abstract: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM inference and environment interaction, we present coordinated optimizations to reduce batch makespan, the time required to complete all tasks in a batch. For hybrid LLMs, a workload-based resource model guides GPU-memory allocation between key-value (KV) cache and recurrent state and provides a reference sample concurrency to exploit parallelism while limiting recomputation. Trajectory-aware routing and scheduling promote cache reuse while balancing worker load. papers.title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
papers.abstract: Streaming video understanding aims to continuously process incoming visual observations, making the retention and retrieval of relevant information increasingly important as the video history grows. Although existing benchmarks include memory-related questions, question-answering accuracy alone does not reliably measure memory capabilities. Incorrect predictions may arise from failures in visual understanding rather than forgetting, whereas correct predictions may rely on linguistic priors or recent observations without requiring historical memory. To address these ambiguities, we introduce MemInStream, a benchmark dedicated to evaluating memory capabilities in streaming video understanding. We develop an evidence-controlled validation protocol that associates each question with temporally localized evidence intervals. The protocol validates evidence solvability and memory necessity by r

papers.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion generation is emerging as a competitive alternative to autoregressive generation by denoising the entire token sequence through iterative refinement. Its global planning and progressive correction capabilities are particularly well suited to autonomous driving. However, transferring this generation paradigm from general-purpose settings to driving introduces substantial domain gaps in both training and inference. To unlock its potential, we propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for standard vision-language model architectures, without auxiliary action experts or specialized mixture-of-experts Transformer, spanning post-training and inference. During supervised fine-tuning, we optimize the representation of planning inputs to suppress hallucinations in task responses. During reinforcement learning, we introduce metric-guided diversity filtering to identify stronge

papers.title: Towards Better Legal Reasoning LLMs: Signal Balancing and Reward Scheduling
papers.abstract: In the legal domain, LLMs can improve reliability and interpretability by generating explicit reasoning traces. However, training LLMs to produce high-quality reasoning traces remains challenging. Existing supervised fine-tuning methods struggle when reasoning traces are significantly longer than final answers, as the learning signal for the answer becomes diluted. Meanwhile, reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization also have several limitations, including costly reward design, performance plateaus, and reward hacking. We therefore propose a two-stage training framework. In Stage I, JurisCoT-SFT employs a length-normalized dual objective to balance learning signals between reasoning traces and final answers. In Stage II, Lifecycle-Aware Backtrackable Policy Optimization dynamically evaluates and retires auxiliary reward signals based on their impact on fi

papers.title: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features
papers.abstract: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Core (26K), TRIDENT-Edge (19K) and WildJailbreak (262K), in overall performance on four safety and five over-refusal benchmarks. Through ablation experim

papers.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We run reinforcement learning (RL) with GRPO across four environments, starting from a supervised fine-tuned 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages. We compare the model before and after RL across 34 benchmarks in one evaluation campaign. MATH improves by 36.07 points, and most Indic benchmarks also improve. Yet XQuAD-Indic F1 falls 19.32 points as English answers rise from 8.7% to 91.7%; IndicQA falls 8.64, while English XQuAD gains 11.71 F1. A second RL run from the same supervised initialization adds an Indic environment together with language and repetition rewards. Compared with the released model, it improves both passage-answering and instruction-following benchmarks, along with preserving MATH performance. papers.title: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has shifted the alignment paradigm of large language models from subjective preference to objective correctness, yet a fundamental disconnect persists between exploration diversity and reasoning validity. Existing strategies predominantly rely on "blind" entropy metrics, e.g., token-level or global sequence-level entropy, which structurally fail to distinguish between effective reasoning and potential hallucinations. This misalignment creates an illusion of diversity, where high entropy tends to signal chaotic degeneration rather than valuable exploration. To bridge this gap, we introduce Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy concept that quantifies diversity exclusively within the valid subspace and systematically filters out the noise of incorrect trajectories. Built on this concept, we instantiate VEPO, a simple Validity-aware Entro

papers.title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
papers.abstract: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. Effective protection must distinguish between requests that may be sent after sanitization and those that must be withheld, while preserving the information needed for authorized tasks. We present GuardianAgentFlow, a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing Web requests through an explicit release contract. A dedicated restriction check grounds permission in the user's instruction; a shared protection scope aligns rewriting with disclosure checking; and candidate-grounded feedback guides revision before transmission. Experiments on Web requests with human-reviewed intent labels show improved request-contract success, while controlled comparisons and role ablations identify the contributions of restriction handling, policy evidence, and candidate checking. papers.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency
papers.abstract: Optional reasoning, retrieval, web search, and tool use can improve large language model responses but incur unnecessary computation when activated indiscriminately. This study investigates whether prompt optimization can compensate for limited router capacity and whether classification gains translate into downstream efficiency. The proposed framework uses prompt-driven small language models to make four independent capability decisions, allowing multiple capabilities to be selected per query. Qwen2.5 routers ranging from 1.5B to 14B parameters are compared across five prompting strategies, followed by an evaluation of capability-specific optimized configurations using a fixed GPT-OSS-120B downstream model on 127 questions. Under minimal prompting, increasing router capacity does not consistently improve classification performance. Prompt optimization narrows the capacity gap for reason

papers.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's already-correct actions. We introduce JudgeMix, a judge-guided data synthesis framework that dynamically interleaves the target model and expert base

papers.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation. papers.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
papers.abstract: Remasking allows diffusion language models to revisit generated text, but effective correction requires knowing when and what to revise. Our diagnosis on Sudoku reveals two gaps. Hidden states contain error information that token confidence does not reliably expose, and remasking an isolated error usually reproduces it when the surrounding context remains fixed. These findings motivate DiVR , a verifier that predicts whether a partially generated sequence will reach a correct answer. Trained on the final correctness of the model's own trajectories, DiVR decides when to regenerate a block and which alternative to retain, while the generator itself stays unchanged. On five reasoning benchmarks with LLaDA-8B-Base, DiVR raises the average accuracy of the fine-tuned generator from 35.3\% to 43.4\% at $1.9$-$3.5\times$ the cost of greedy decoding, above search baselines that use $3.8$-$7.4\tim

papers.title: Gravity and Flight: Learning to Navigate Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Scenes
papers.abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly capable, yet their reasoning in complex remote sensing scenes can remain coarse-grained and insufficiently grounded in task-relevant visual evidence. We propose Gravity and Flight (G&F), a framework for scene specialization with limited supervision that separates visual and reasoning verification while coupling policy updates. It combines Evidence-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning (EoT-SFT) and Relational Transfer Policy Optimization (RTPO). EoT-SFT teaches fine-grained observation and faithful reasoning through description, analysis, and supported conclusions. RTPO independently samples responses to scene-matched image pairs with fine-grained visual differences under a shared task. papers.title: Any Channel Count, One Token Stream: Incorporating Spatial Audio Understanding and Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models
papers.abstract: Audio phase relations encode source locations, yet existing large audio-language models (LALM) reduce audio to single-channel content to stabilise general audio understanding, leaving spatial information for direction, distance, and source-relation questions unused. We present SpheraAudio, which accepts recordings with any channel count -- mono, stereo, First-Order Ambisonics (FOA), or higher -- and maps them into a single token stream. A spatial encoder turns complex multichannel spectra into spatial tokens interleaved with audio tokens at corresponding temporal positions. Spatial Multimodal RoPE (SMRoPE) makes each token's modality identity and temporal slot visible to rotary attention without altering the language model's original RoPE. papers.title: MLIRBench - A Benchmark and Dataset for Compiler and Hardware-Aware Reasoning
papers.abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly popular in software engineering and have performed well on different programming tasks. However, it is still difficult to know whether these models truly understand program behavior or whether they mainly rely on patterns learned from their training data. This distinction is particularly important for intermediate representations (IRs), where operations, dataflow, and execution semantics are explicitly represented. In this paper, we introduce MLIRBench, a benchmark for evaluating how LLMs reason about MLIR programs. MLIRBench uses a multi-agent pipeline to generate program mutations, validate their behavior through execution, and construct reasoning tasks from torch and linalg program pairs. The dataset contains 1,768 validated pairs, including 888 linalg pairs and 880 torch pairs, labeled as EQUIV, DIVERGE, or ERROR.

papers.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
papers.abstract: Large language models trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) with verifiable rewards exhibit strong reasoning ability and broad generalization, whereas models trained with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) are often viewed as more prone to memorization and limited transfer. This paper rethinks this distinction through the lens of SFT training data on widely used Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 series models. First, we study the role of data source and show that it is critical: a carefully mixed SFT dataset substantially outperforms data generated solely by a larger model. Second, we study the role of data scale and show that matching the number of correct rollouts between SFT and RL greatly improves SFT generalization, while matching the total rollout budget enables SFT to generalize as well as RL. papers.title: Sophon: A Procedural Diagnostic for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Open-weight Vision-Language Models (VLMs) score 85-94% on spatial benchmarks (BLINK Spatial, What's Up CLEVR) yet collapse to chance on simple geometric questions when object, scene, and texture priors are stripped away. We introduce and open-source Sophon, a procedurally generated diagnostic of paired colored point-cloud stimuli across three coordinate systems (1D linear, 2D Cartesian, 2D polar) and four question types (binary, categorical, comparative, quantitative). Across four open architectures (LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OneVision, Qwen2.5-VL, Idefics3), accuracy clusters at 47-52% while frontier models (Opus 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.4) clear 77-83% and humans reach 84-94%. We use linear probes and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to trace the open-weight failures. papers.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. papers.title: Scale-Induced Semantic Shift in Visual Prompt Injection Against VLMs and Web Agents
papers.abstract: Visual content in multimedia systems may be resized, compressed, or re-rendered before it is interpreted by a vision-language model. We study a security failure mode in which these transformations change the machine-readable semantics of an image: a textual instruction is not recovered at a $512\times512$ presentation resolution under our evaluation protocol but becomes recoverable after aggressive downsampling. We formulate this behavior as Scale-Induced Semantic Shift (SISS) and develop a closed-loop black-box framework that combines dual-scale verification, selective self-hardening, shallow-layer low-rank adaptation, and pixel-space noise regularization. On a fixed 300-case benchmark, the third SISS refinement round obtains a $58.75\%$ average attack success rate across four closed-source vision-language models, compared with $41.08\%$ for the strongest generation baseline. papers.title: Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning can teach vision-language models (VLMs) to decline harmful image-text requests, but how safe the result becomes is set indirectly, through reward weights found by trial runs. Stating safety as budgets on the rate of harmful assistance and the rate of over-refusal, enforced by Lagrange multipliers inside GRPO with an off-the-shelf scorer as the cost, is the natural fix, and it fails twice. The multiplier compares the scorer's mean with the budget, and scorers built for ranking get the mean wrong: a fixed-point analysis shows that the mean bias, not the budget, then decides whether the multiplier settles, saturates or switches off. And standard GRPO standardizes the penalized reward within each group, which cancels the multiplier before it reaches the gradient. papers.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Enterprise agents accumulate memory across dozens of sessions in which facts contradict, get superseded, and blur as similarly named entities collide in embedding space. The field treats this as a retrieval problem; we show it is not. On ENT-310, a synthetic enterprise sales-agent memory benchmark of 310 queries (210 answerable, 100 unanswerable), a vanilla Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) reader over a memory store already matches strong memory systems on the recall pillars. Retention and currency are near-saturated, roughly 0.93 to 0.98 for every competent system, so recall is essentially solved. What remains unsolved is resolution: which entity a query refers to, which time-state is current, and whether to commit an answer at all or decline when evidence is insufficient.
